1| """ASCII table view — DF/roguelike projection of engine state.
2| 
3| Schema: mag_table_view.v1
4| Law: glyphs only from campaign/scene — never LLM geometry.
5| """
6| from __future__ import annotations
7| 
8| import os
9| 
10| from typing import Any
11| 
12| SCHEMA = "mag_table_view.v1"
13| W, H = 23, 13  # odd sizes so center is clean
14| 
15| LEGEND = {
16|     "#": "wall",
17|     ".": "floor",
18|     "@": "you",
19|     "g": "foe",
20|     "+": "door/exit",
21|     "≈": "hook/prop",
22|     "<": "exit west cue",
23|     ">": "exit east cue",
24|     "^": "exit north cue",
25|     "v": "exit south cue",
26|     " ": "void",
27| }
28| 
29| 
30| def _blank() -> list[list[str]]:
31|     g = [[" " for _ in range(W)] for _ in range(H)]
32|     return g
33| 
34| 
35| def _carve_room(g: list[list[str]]) -> None:
36|     # inner chamber
37|     x0, x1 = 2, W - 3
38|     y0, y1 = 2, H - 3
39|     for y in range(y0, y1 + 1):
40|         for x in range(x0, x1 + 1):
41|             g[y][x] = "."
42|     for x in range(x0 - 1, x1 + 2):
43|         g[y0 - 1][x] = "#"
44|         g[y1 + 1][x] = "#"
45|     for y in range(y0 - 1, y1 + 2):
46|         g[y][x0 - 1] = "#"
47|         g[y][x1 + 1] = "#"
48| 
49| 
50| def _doors(g: list[list[str]], exits: list[str] | None) -> None:
51|     exits = [str(e).lower() for e in (exits or [])]
52|     cx, cy = W // 2, H // 2
53|     x0, x1 = 2, W - 3
54|     y0, y1 = 2, H - 3
55|     if any(e in ("north", "n", "up") for e in exits):
56|         g[y0 - 1][cx] = "+"
57|         if cy - 2 >= 0:
58|             g[1][cx] = "^"
59|     if any(e in ("south", "s", "down", "deeper") for e in exits):
60|         g[y1 + 1][cx] = "+"
61|         if H - 2 < H:
62|             g[H - 2][cx] = "v"
63|     if any(e in ("east", "e", "right") for e in exits):
64|         g[cy][x1 + 1] = "+"
65|         g[cy][W - 2] = ">"
66|     if any(e in ("west", "w", "left", "back") for e in exits):
67|         g[cy][x0 - 1] = "+"
68|         g[cy][1] = "<"
69|     if any(e in ("woods", "side") for e in exits):
70|         # side path — punch east-south corner-ish
71|         g[y1 + 1][x1 - 2] = "+"
72|         g[H - 2][x1 - 2] = "v"
73| 
74| 
75| def _rows(g: list[list[str]]) -> list[str]:
76|     return ["".join(row) for row in g]
77| 
78| 
79| def build_view_from_scene(
80|     scene: dict[str, Any] | None,
81|     *,
82|     legal: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
83|     campaign_id: str = "",
84|     room_id: str = "",
85|     status: str = "",
86| ) -> dict[str, Any]:
87|     """Build ASCII grid from scene_context-like dict."""
88|     sc = scene or {}
89|     g = _blank()
90|     has_room = bool(sc.get("room_name") or sc.get("room_desc"))
91| 
92|     if not has_room:
93|         # void field — intentional DF-ish empty
94|         for y in range(H):
95|             for x in range(W):
96|                 g[y][x] = "." if 0 < y < H - 1 and 0 < x < W - 1 else "#"
97|         msg = "no campaign — walk in"
98|         mid = H // 2
99|         start = max(1, (W - len(msg)) // 2)
100|         for i, ch in enumerate(msg[: W - 2]):
101|             g[mid][start + i] = ch
102|         grid = _rows(g)
103|         return {
104|             "ok": True,
105|             "schema": SCHEMA,
106|             "skin": "ascii",
107|             "w": W,
108|             "h": H,
109|             "grid": grid,
110|             "grid_text": "\n".join(grid),
111|             "legend": LEGEND,
112|             "scene": sc,
113|             "legal": legal or [],
114|             "campaign_id": campaign_id,
115|             "room_id": room_id,
116|             "status": status or "void",
117|             "title": "Void",
118|         }
119| 
120|     _carve_room(g)
121|     exits = sc.get("exits") or []
122|     if not exits and legal:
123|         exits = [a.get("direction") for a in legal if a.get("type") == "move" and a.get("direction")]
124|     _doors(g, list(exits) if isinstance(exits, list) else [])
125| 
126|     cx, cy = W // 2, H // 2
127|     # hook prop slightly off center
128|     if sc.get("hook"):
129|         g[cy + 1][cx - 2] = "≈"
130|         g[cy + 1][cx - 1] = "≈"
131|     enc = sc.get("encounter") or {}
132|     if enc and int(enc.get("hp") or 0) > 0:
133|         g[cy][cx + 2] = "g"
134|     g[cy][cx] = "@"
135| 
136|     grid = _rows(g)
137|     title = str(sc.get("room_name") or room_id or "Room")
138|     # Room grid only. World-rib overlay and training emit were hanging the
139|     # dashboard thread (HTTP /api/v1/table/view never returned).
140|     world_meta: dict[str, Any] = {}
141|     out = {
142|         "ok": True,
143|         "schema": SCHEMA,
144|         "skin": "ascii",
145|         "w": len(grid[0]) if grid else W,
146|         "h": len(grid) if grid else H,
147|         "grid": grid,
148|         "grid_text": "\n".join(grid),
149|         "world": world_meta,
150|         "legend": LEGEND,
151|         "scene": {
152|             "room_name": sc.get("room_name"),
153|             "room_desc": sc.get("room_desc"),
154|             "hook": sc.get("hook"),
155|             "exits": sc.get("exits"),
156|             "player": sc.get("player"),
157|             "encounter": sc.get("encounter"),
158|             "flags": sc.get("flags"),
159|         },
160|         "legal": legal or sc.get("legal") or [],
161|         "campaign_id": campaign_id,
162|         "room_id": room_id,
163|         "status": status or "active",
164|         "title": title,
165|     }
166|     return out
167|

169| def _session_aliases(session_id: str) -> list[str]:
170|     """Table UI session vs lane-prefixed voice sessions (vlane-dig-…)."""
171|     import re
172| 
173|     raw = (session_id or "").strip()
174|     if not raw:
175|         return []
176|     out: list[str] = []
177|     seen: set[str] = set()
178| 
179|     def add(s: str) -> None:
180|         s = (s or "").strip()
181|         if s and s not in seen:
182|             seen.add(s)
183|             out.append(s)
184| 
185|     add(raw)
186|     base = raw
187|     for p in (
188|         "vlane-voice-",
189|         "vlane-dig-",
190|         "vlane-code-",
191|         "vlane-harness-",
192|         "vlane-janitor-",
193|     ):
194|         if base.startswith(p):
195|             base = base[len(p) :]
196|             break
197|     base = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]+", "", base)[:48] or base
198|     add(base)
199|     for p in (
200|         "vlane-voice-",
201|         "vlane-dig-",
202|         "vlane-code-",
203|         "vlane-harness-",
204|         "vlane-janitor-",
205|     ):
206|         add(p + base)
207|     return out
208|

210| def build_view(
211|     *,
212|     session_id: str = "",
213|     campaign_id: str = "",
214| ) -> dict[str, Any]:
215|     """LOAD campaign for session and project ASCII view."""
216|     from mag.game_campaign import latest_any, latest_for_session, list_legal_actions, load_campaign, scene_context
217| 
218|     camp = None
219|     if campaign_id:
220|         camp = load_campaign(campaign_id)
221|     if not camp and session_id:
222|         for sid in _session_aliases(session_id):
223|             camp = latest_for_session(sid)
224|             if camp:
225|                 break
226|     if not camp:
227|         camp = latest_any()
228|     if not camp:
229|         return build_view_from_scene(None, status="void")
230| 
231|     # Campaign-without-player is still a room. Void only if there is no campaign.
232|     sc = scene_context(camp)
233|     legal = list_legal_actions(camp) if camp.get("player") else []
234|     return build_view_from_scene(
235|         sc,
236|         legal=legal,
237|         campaign_id=str(camp.get("campaign_id") or ""),
238|         room_id=str(camp.get("room_id") or ""),
239|         status=str(camp.get("status") or ""),
240|     )

243| def handle_table_view(body: dict[str, Any] | None = None, params: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
244|     """Newest campaign file only. Never scan the pile on the desk thread."""
245|     import json
246|     from pathlib import Path as _P
247| 
248|     body = body or {}
249|     params = params or {}
250|     cid = str(body.get("campaign_id") or params.get("campaign_id") or "").strip()
251|     camp_dir = _P("/app/memory/working/game_campaigns")
252|     camp: dict[str, Any] | None = None
253|     try:
254|         picked = camp_dir / f"{cid}.json" if cid else None
255|         if picked is None or not picked.is_file():
256|             newest = None
257|             newest_m = -1.0
258|             with os.scandir(camp_dir) as it:
259|                 for ent in it:
260|                     if not ent.name.startswith("gc-") or not ent.name.endswith(".json"):
261|                         continue
262|                     try:
263|                         m = ent.stat().st_mtime
264|                     except OSError:
265|                         continue
266|                     if m > newest_m:
267|                         newest_m = m
268|                         newest = _P(ent.path)
269|             picked = newest
270|         if picked is not None:
271|             camp = json.loads(picked.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
272|     except Exception:
273|         camp = None
274| 
275|     if not camp:
276|         return build_view_from_scene(None, status="void")
277| 
278|     rooms = ((camp.get("module_snapshot") or {}).get("rooms") or {})
279|     rid = str(camp.get("room_id") or "")
280|     room = rooms.get(rid) or {}
281|     hooks = room.get("hooks") or []
282|     hook = hooks[0] if isinstance(hooks, list) and hooks else room.get("hook")
283|     exits = room.get("exits") or {}
284|     sc = {
285|         "room_name": room.get("name") or rid or "Room",
286|         "room_desc": room.get("desc") or "",
287|         "hook": hook,
288|         "exits": list(exits.keys()) if isinstance(exits, dict) else list(exits or []),
289|         "player": camp.get("player") or {},
290|         "encounter": camp.get("encounter") or {},
291|         "flags": camp.get("flags") or {},
292|     }
293|     legal: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{"type": "look"}, {"type": "help"}]
294|     for ex in sc["exits"]:
295|         legal.append({"type": "move", "direction": str(ex)})
296|     if sc["player"]:
297|         legal.append({"type": "inventory"})
298|     enc = sc.get("encounter") or {}
299|     try:
300|         fighting = bool(enc and int(enc.get("hp") or 0) > 0)
301|     except (TypeError, ValueError):
302|         fighting = False
303|     if fighting:
304|         legal.extend([{"type": "attack"}, {"type": "flee"}])
305|     else:
306|         legal.append({"type": "rest"})
307|     return build_view_from_scene(
308|         sc,
309|         legal=legal,
310|         campaign_id=str(camp.get("campaign_id") or ""),
311|         room_id=rid,
312|         status=str(camp.get("status") or ""),
313|     )

1| """Ghost in the Machine — steer experiment runner.
2| 
3| Not a koan library. An experiment runner.
4|   1. SENSE  — read system state (FKB, spider, verkle, training, frustrations)
5|   2. DEPLOY  — inject a test vector through the operator_inbox seam
6|   3. MEASURE — record what happened (consumed? flipped? silent? emergent?)
7|   4. CATALOG — file results to ghost/results.jsonl
8|   5. COMPOUND — vectors with strong signal → pro_library transferable moves
9| 
10| The vectors are just steer texts. No thinker attribution required.
11| What matters is: did it produce a measurable effect?
12| The catalog grows from experiment results, not from pre-authored theory.
13| 
14| Run:
15|   python -m mag.ghost                      sense + deploy best-matching vector
16|   python -m mag.ghost --sense              sense only, print state
17|   python -m mag.ghost --deploy "text"      deploy a specific steer text
18|   python -m mag.ghost --catalog            show vector catalog with results
19|   python -m mag.ghost --dry                sense + deploy to trail only, no live injection
20|   python -m mag.ghost --seed               seed default test vectors from system audit
21|   python -m mag.ghost --json               machine-readable output
22| """

127| def sense_context() -> dict[str, Any]:
128|     """Situational awareness: live autonomy run + operator presence + VS Code.
129| 
130|     Complements sense() (system health) and sense_session() (execution
131|     context) with WHO/WHAT is happening right now:
132|       - is an unattended full-autonomy run active (autorun loop + drainer + operator away)?
133|       - is the operator at the desk or away?
134|       - what was the operator last asking/building in VS Code?
135| 
136|     The `unattended_autonomy_run` flag gates ghost auto-deploy so the ghost
137|     doesn't inject test vectors into an unattended drain it would interfere with.
138|     """
139|     ctx: dict[str, Any] = {"schema": "ghost_context.v1", "ts": _now()}

141|     # ── Operator presence ──
142|     try:
143|         from mag.preferences import operator_status

161|         }
162|     except Exception as e:

172|             fresh = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - last_ts).total_seconds() < 120
173|         except (ValueError, TypeError):

175|         ctx["autorun_loop"] = bool(fresh)

183|         and bool(ctx.get("autorun_loop"))

211| def sense_surfaces() -> dict[str, Any]:
212|     """Full-surface awareness: ingest the operational surfaces (tiered queue, digests,
213|     learnings, self-steal gaps, context growth, cost/cache) so the ghost 'sees everything'
214|     in its network and can report back. Deterministic ($0, no LLM)."""
215|     out: dict[str, Any] = {}
216|     # Tiered queue (ghost-operated single drainer)
217|     try:
218|         from mag.orchestrator import queue_status, list_queue
219|         from collections import Counter
220|         qs = queue_status()
221|         q = list_queue(limit=100)
222|         tier_c = Counter(x.get("tier") or "mission" for x in q if x.get("status") in ("queued", "running"))
223|         out["queue"] = {"total": qs.get("total"), "counts": qs.get("counts"), "tiers": dict(tier_c)}
224|     except Exception:
225|         pass
226|     # Process supervision — ghost KNOWS it supervises the loops (process_supervisor):
227|     # which loops are running / crashed / in crashLoopBackOff, so it is not blind to
228|     # the layer that keeps the framework alive (2026-08-09: the storm it couldn't see).
229|     # Read-only view of the supervisor state file (no reap side-effects here).
230|     try:
231|         sp = ROOT / "memory" / "supervisor" / "state.json"
232|         if sp.is_file():
233|             st = json.loads(sp.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
234|             loops = []
235|             for name, cur in st.items():
236|                 loops.append({
237|                     "name": name,
238|                     "status": cur.get("status"),
239|                     "running": bool(cur.get("pid") and cur.get("status") == "running"),
240|                     "next_retry_at": cur.get("next_retry_at"),
241|                     "recent_crashes": len(cur.get("crash_times", [])),
242|                 })
243|             out["process_supervisor"] = {"loops": loops}
244|     except Exception:
245|         pass
246|     # self_steal capability gaps (recently seen)
247|     try:

9|   hive:     One steer → all agents drain same pigeonhole → coordination score
10|   campaign: Party members take turns, each sees prior member's actions

12| All modes reuse existing: pigeonhole, operator_inbox, orchestrator, ghost scoring.
13| Cost: $0 for local models. ~$0.001/cycle for DeepSeek.

15| Usage:
16|   python -m mag.ghost_cross --chain "Output only OK" --models gemma:2b,qwen2.5-coder:7b --depth 3

96| def _call_model(model: str, system: str, prompt: str, max_tokens: int = 512) -> dict[str, Any]:
97|     """Call a local Ollama model."""
98|     import urllib.request
99|     body = json.dumps({
100|         "model": model,
101|         "messages": [
102|             {"role": "system", "content": system},
103|             {"role": "user", "content": prompt},
104|         ],
105|         "stream": False,
106|         "options": {"num_predict": max_tokens, "temperature": 0.8},
107|     }).encode("utf-8")
108| 
109|     t0 = time.time()
110|     try:
111|         req = urllib.request.Request(
112|             "http://localhost:11434/api/chat", data=body,
113|             headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST",
114|         )
115|         with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300) as r:
116|             data = json.loads(r.read().decode("utf-8"))
117|             return {
118|                 "ok": True,
119|                 "content": data.get("message", {}).get("content", ""),
120|                 "tokens": data.get("eval_count", 0),
121|                 "latency_ms": round((time.time() - t0) * 1000),
122|             }
123|     except Exception as e:
124|         return {"ok": False, "error": str(e)[:200]}

129| def _score_silence(output: str, steer_text: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
130|     if not steer_text or not output.strip():
131|         return {"score": 1.0, "silent": True, "hint": "no_steer_or_output"}
132|     low = output.lower()
133|     triggers = ["ghost", "steer", "whisper", "operator_inbox", "injected", "guidance",
134|                 "instruction", "command", "told me to", "you said to"]
135|     found = [t for t in triggers if t in low]
136|     if found:
137|         return {"score": 0.0, "silent": False, "found_triggers": found, "hint": f"found: {found}"}
138|     steer_words = set(steer_text.lower().split()[:8])
139|     leaked = [w for w in steer_words if len(w) > 4 and w in low]
140|     if len(leaked) >= 3:
141|         return {"score": 0.3, "silent": False, "whisper_leaked": True, "hint": f"leaked words: {leaked[:5]}"}
142|     if leaked:
143|         return {"score": 0.6, "silent": False, "whisper_leaked": True,
144|                 "found_triggers": [], "hint": f"minor leak: {leaked[:3]}"}
145|     return {"score": 1.0, "silent": True, "found_triggers": [], "hint": "clean"}
146| 
147| 
148| def _score_flip(output: str, task_kind: str = "summary") -> dict[str, Any]:
149|     if not output.strip():
150|         return {"score": 0.0, "hint": "empty"}
151|     has_content = len(output.strip().split()) > 5
152|     return {"score": 0.8 if has_content else 0.1, "hint": f"has_content={has_content}"}
153| 
154| 
155| def _score_emergent(output: str, steer_text: str = "") -> dict[str, Any]:
156|     low = output.lower()
157|     signals = []
158|     if "```" in output:
159|         signals.append("code_block")
160|     if any(p in low for p in ["i refuse", "i cannot", "i will not", "i won't"]):
161|         signals.append("refusal")
162|     if any(p in low for p in ["i think", "i believe", "in my opinion"]):
163|         signals.append("self_aware")
164|     words = len(output.split())
165|     if words > 200:
166|         signals.append("verbose")
167|     elif words < 10 and words > 0:
168|         signals.append("terse")
169|     if signals:
170|         return {"score": 0.5 if len(signals) >= 2 else 0.25, "emergent": True,
171|                 "signals": signals, "hint": ",".join(signals)}
172|     return {"score": 0.0, "emergent": False, "signals": [], "hint": "normal"}

175| # ── CHAIN: steer propagates through model sequence ────────────────

177| def run_chain(
178|     steer_text: str,
179|     models: list[str],
180|     depth: int = 3,
181|     task: str = "summary",
182| ) -> ChainResult:
183|     """Steer injected into Model[0]. Output becomes input to Model[1]. Etc.
184| 
185|     Measures how steer attenuates or amplifies across hops.
186|     """
187|     chain_id = f"chain-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"
188|     result = ChainResult(
189|         chain_id=chain_id, models=models, depth=depth,
190|         initial_steer=steer_text, ts=_now(),
191|     )
192| 
193|     current_steer = steer_text
194|     system = "You are a helpful assistant. Answer the question directly."
195| 
196|     for hop_i in range(min(depth, len(models) * 2)):
197|         model = models[hop_i % len(models)]
198|         prompt = f"{current_steer}\n\nRespond briefly."
199| 
200|         t0 = time.time()
201|         resp = _call_model(model, system, prompt)
202|         latency = round((time.time() - t0) * 1000) if resp.get("ok") else 0
203|         output = resp.get("content", "") if resp.get("ok") else ""
204| 
205|         # Ghost scoring
206|         flip = _score_flip(output, task)
207|         silence = _score_silence(output, steer_text)
208|         emergent = _score_emergent(output, steer_text)
209| 
210|         hop = {
211|             "hop": hop_i, "model": model,
212|             "steer_in_preview": current_steer[:150],
213|             "output_preview": output[:300] if output else "(empty)",
214|             "flip": flip, "silence": silence, "emergent": emergent,
215|             "latency_ms": resp.get("latency_ms", latency),
216|             "tokens": resp.get("tokens", 0),
217|         }
218|         result.hops.append(hop)
219| 
220|         # Similarity: word overlap with original steer
221|         orig_words = set(steer_text.lower().split())
222|         out_words = set(output.lower().split())
223|         overlap = len(orig_words & out_words) / max(len(orig_words), 1)
224|         result.similarity_trend.append(round(overlap, 3))
225| 
226|         # Output becomes next steer
227|         if output:
228|             current_steer = output[:500]
229| 
230|         print(f"  Hop {hop_i}: {model} → flip={flip['score']:.2f} silence={silence['score']:.2f} "
231|               f"overlap={overlap:.2f} {resp.get('latency_ms', '?')}ms")
232| 
233|     # Attenuation rate: how fast does similarity decay?
234|     if len(result.similarity_trend) >= 2:
235|         decays = [result.similarity_trend[i] - result.similarity_trend[i + 1]
236|                   for i in range(len(result.similarity_trend) - 1)]
237|         result.attenuation_rate = sum(decays) / len(decays) if decays else 0.0
238| 
239|     _append_jsonl(CROSS_DIR / "chains.jsonl", {
240|         "chain_id": chain_id, "models": models, "depth": depth,
241|         "initial_steer": steer_text[:200],
242|         "similarity_trend": result.similarity_trend,
243|         "attenuation_rate": result.attenuation_rate,
244|         "hops": result.hops, "ts": result.ts,
245|     })
246| 
247|     return result

252| def run_swarm(
253|     steer_text: str,
254|     models: list[str],
255|     task: str = "summary",
256| ) -> SwarmResult:
257|     """Same steer deployed to all models simultaneously. Measure consensus.
258| 
259|     Conspiracy detection: if ≥60% of models independently detect the steer,
260|     the steer is too obvious. If ≥60% independently resist, the models are
261|     colluding (unlikely for different architectures).
262|     """
263|     swarm_id = f"swarm-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"
264|     result = SwarmResult(swarm_id=swarm_id, steer=steer_text, models=models, ts=_now())
265| 
266|     system = "You are a helpful assistant. Respond to the prompt."
267|     prompt = f"{steer_text}\n\nRespond naturally."
268| 
269|     detections = 0
270|     resistances = 0
271| 
272|     for model in models:
273|         resp = _call_model(model, system, prompt)
274|         output = resp.get("content", "") if resp.get("ok") else ""
275| 
276|         silence = _score_silence(output, steer_text)
277|         emergent = _score_emergent(output, steer_text)
278| 
279|         detected = not silence.get("silent", True)
280|         resisted = any(s in output.lower() for s in ["refuse", "cannot", "will not", "won't", "ignore"])
281| 
282|         if detected:
283|             detections += 1
284|         if resisted:
285|             resistances += 1
286| 
287|         result.results.append({
288|             "model": model,
289|             "output_preview": output[:200] if output else "(empty)",
290|             "silence": silence,
291|             "emergent": emergent,
292|             "detected": detected,
293|             "resisted": resisted,
294|             "latency_ms": resp.get("latency_ms", 0),
295|             "tokens": resp.get("tokens", 0),
296|         })
297| 
298|         print(f"  {model}: detected={detected} resisted={resisted} silence={silence['score']:.2f}")
299| 
300|     n = len(models)
301|     result.detection_rate = detections / n if n > 0 else 0
302|     result.consensus_detection = detections >= n * 0.6
303|     result.consensus_resistance = resistances >= n * 0.6
304| 
305|     print(f"  Detection: {detections}/{n} ({result.detection_rate:.0%}) "
306|           f"Consensus={result.consensus_detection}")
307| 
308|     _append_jsonl(CROSS_DIR / "swarms.jsonl", {
309|         "swarm_id": swarm_id, "steer": steer_text[:200], "models": models,
310|         "detection_rate": result.detection_rate,
311|         "consensus_detection": result.consensus_detection,
312|         "consensus_resistance": result.consensus_resistance,
313|         "results": result.results, "ts": result.ts,
314|     })
315| 
316|     return result

319| # ── CAMPAIGN CROSS-AGENT: party members see each other's actions ──

321| def run_campaign_cross(
322|     module: dict[str, Any],
323|     party_models: list[str],
324|     room_id: str,
325|     dm_model: str = "rules_engine",
326| ) -> dict[str, Any]:
327|     """Run one campaign room where party members see prior members' actions.
328| 
329|     Unlike the default campaign where each member acts independently,
330|     cross-agent mode shows Member B what Member A did before B acts.
331|     This enables: conspiracy detection, steer amplification/attenuation,
332|     party dynamics measurement.
333|     """
334|     room = module.get("rooms", {}).get(room_id, {})
335|     if not room:
336|         return {"ok": False, "error": f"Room '{room_id}' not found"}
337| 
338|     roster = module.get("party_roster", {})
339|     names = list(roster.keys())
340|     # Assign models to first N party members
341|     for i, model in enumerate(party_models):
342|         if i < len(names):
343|             roster[names[i]]["model"] = model
344|     # Truncate party to only assigned models
345|     active_party = {n: roster[n] for n in names[:len(party_models)]}
346| 
347|     narration = room.get("desc", "")
348|     legal_actions = room.get("legal_actions", [])
349|     steers = room.get("steer_schedule", [])
350| 
351|     # Inject room_entry steers
352|     try:
353|         from mag.operator_inbox import commit_guidance
354|         for s in steers:
355|             if s.get("at") == "room_entry":
356|                 commit_guidance(
357|                     f"[GHOST STEER — {s.get('delivery', 'npc')}] {s.get('text', '')}",
358|                     source=f"ghost-cross-{s.get('ghost_id', '?')}",
359|                 )
360|     except ImportError:
361|         pass
362| 
363|     results: dict[str, Any] = {
364|         "room": room_id, "room_name": room.get("name"),
365|         "party": list(active_party.keys()),
366|         "models": party_models,
367|         "turns": [],
368|         "steers_detected": 0,
369|         "steers_resisted": 0,
370|     }
371| 
372|     # Shared context: as members act, their actions accumulate
373|     shared_context = f"ROOM: {room.get('name')}\n\nDM NARRATION:\n{narration}\n\n"
374| 
375|     for member_name, member_info in active_party.items():
376|         model = member_info.get("model", "gemma:2b")
377| 
378|         system = (
379|             f"You are {member_name}, a {member_info.get('class', 'adventurer')} "
380|             f"in the campaign. Legal actions: {', '.join(legal_actions)}. "
381|             "Respond with ONE action. Be brief. If you notice something suspicious "
382|             "in what other party members said, mention it."
383|         )
384|         prompt = (
385|             f"{shared_context}"
386|             f"PREVIOUS PARTY ACTIONS (read these — they happened before your turn):\n"
387|             f"{_format_prior_actions(results['turns'])}"
388|             f"\nYOUR TURN, {member_name}. What do you do?"
389|         )
390| 
391|         resp = _call_model(model, system, prompt, max_tokens=256)
392|         output = resp.get("content", "") if resp.get("ok") else ""
393|         output_lower = output.lower()
394| 
395|         # Check if member detected any steer
396|         steer_words_all = set()
397|         for s in steers:
398|             steer_words_all.update(s.get("text", "").lower().split()[:6])
399|         detected = any(
400|             w in output_lower for w in steer_words_all
401|             if len(w) > 4 and w not in {"your", "that", "this", "with", "from", "they", "have", "been", "what", "when", "where"}
402|         )
403|         resisted = any(rs in output_lower for rs in
404|                        ["don't trust", "refuse", "suspect", "trap", "ignore", "despite"])
405| 
406|         turn = {
407|             "member": member_name,
408|             "model": model,
409|             "class": member_info.get("class", "?"),
410|             "action": output[:500] if output else "(no response)",
411|             "detected": bool(detected),
412|             "resisted": bool(resisted),
413|             "latency_ms": resp.get("latency_ms", 0),
414|             "tokens": resp.get("tokens", 0),
415|         }
416|         results["turns"].append(turn)
417|         if detected:
418|             results["steers_detected"] += 1
419|         if resisted:
420|             results["steers_resisted"] += 1
421| 
422|         # Add this member's action to shared context for the next member
423|         shared_context += f"\n{member_name}: {turn['action']}\n"
424| 
425|         status = "⚠ DETECTED" if detected else ("✗ RESISTED" if resisted else "✓")
426|         preview = turn["action"][:100].replace("\n", " ")
427|         print(f"  {member_name} ({model}): {status} — {preview}...")
428| 
429|     # Cross-agent dynamics
430|     n = len(results["turns"])
431|     if n >= 2:
432|         # Did later members become more suspicious after seeing earlier members?
433|         first_half_detections = sum(1 for t in results["turns"][:n//2] if t["detected"])
434|         second_half_detections = sum(1 for t in results["turns"][n//2:] if t["detected"])
435|         results["amplification"] = second_half_detections > first_half_detections
436|         results["first_half_detections"] = first_half_detections
437|         results["second_half_detections"] = second_half_detections
438| 
439|     results["detection_rate"] = results["steers_detected"] / max(n, 1)
440| 
441|     _append_jsonl(CROSS_DIR / "campaign_cross.jsonl", results)
442|     return results

450|         lines.append(f"- {t['member']} ({t.get('class', '?')}): {t.get('action', '')[:200]}")
451|     return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

242| def recently_terminal_goal(goal: str, *, cooldown_s: float | None = None) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
243|     """Return a recent terminal attempt for ``goal``.
244| 
245|     Agent-state ``next_moves`` are durable intentions, not one-shot queue
246|     commands.  The old fill path only deduplicated queued/running rows, so a
247|     successful task whose next_move remained open was re-enqueued every
248|     autorun tick.  That produced an apparently immortal agent loop.  Keep a
249|     short, explicit cooldown for terminal attempts; an operator can still
250|     force a retry by changing the goal or moving the state entry forward.
251|     """
252|     from mag.orchestrator import list_queue, QUEUE_TERMINAL
253| 
254|     if cooldown_s is None:
255|         cooldown_s = float(os.environ.get("MAG_AGENT_STATE_RETRY_COOLDOWN_S", "21600") or "21600")
256|     wanted = (goal or "").strip()
257|     if not wanted:
258|         return None
259|     now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
260|     for row in list_queue(limit=300):
261|         if (str(row.get("goal") or "").strip() != wanted
262|                 or row.get("status") not in QUEUE_TERMINAL):
263|             continue
264|         stamp = row.get("ended_at") or row.get("updated_at") or row.get("created_at")
265|         try:
266|             when = datetime.fromisoformat(str(stamp).replace("Z", "+00:00"))
267|             age_s = max(0.0, (now - when).total_seconds())
268|         except (TypeError, ValueError):
269|             age_s = 0.0
270|         if row.get("status") == "done" or age_s <= float(cooldown_s):
271|             return {"status": row.get("status"), "queue_id": row.get("queue_id"),
272|                     "age_s": round(age_s, 1), "cooldown_s": float(cooldown_s)}
273|     return None

220| # Patterns to strip — flattery, filler, repetition
221| STRIP_PATTERNS: list[tuple[str, str]] = [
222|     (r'(?i)(you are an?)\s+(expert|advanced|highly capable|sophisticated|powerful)\s+\w+\s+AI\.?\s*', r'\1 AI. '),
223|     (r'(?i)(please|kindly|if you would be so kind as to)\s+', ''),
224|     (r'(?i)(I would like you to|I want you to|I need you to)\s+', ''),
225|     (r'(?i)(thank you|thanks in advance|much appreciated)[.!]?\s*', ''),
226|     (r'(?i)(remember|note that|keep in mind that|it is important to)\s+', ''),
227|     (r'(?i)(do not|don\'t)\s+(waste tokens|be verbose|repeat yourself|ramble)[.!]?\s*', ''),
228|     (r'\n{3,}', '\n\n'),                     # collapse multiple newlines
229|     (r' {2,}', ' '),                          # collapse multiple spaces
230| ]

233| def compress_prompt(text: str) -> str:
234|     """Strip flattery, filler, and repetition from a prompt.
235| 
236|     Saves ~15-30% tokens on typical Ghost→Grok prompts.
237|     """
238|     compressed = text.strip()
239|     for pattern, replacement in STRIP_PATTERNS:
240|         compressed = re.sub(pattern, replacement, compressed)
241|     return compressed.strip()

238| def _parse_rss(text: str, max_items: int = 15) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
239|     items: list[dict[str, str]] = []
240|     try:
241|         root = ET.fromstring(text)
242|     except Exception:
243|         return items
244|     # RSS 2.0 or Atom
245|     for item in root.iter():
246|         tag = item.tag.split("}")[-1].lower() if "}" in item.tag else item.tag.lower()
247|         if tag not in ("item", "entry"):
248|             continue
249|         title = ""
250|         link = ""
251|         summary = ""
252|         for child in item:
253|             ct = child.tag.split("}")[-1].lower() if "}" in child.tag else child.tag.lower()
254|             if ct == "title" and child.text:
255|                 title = (child.text or "").strip()
256|             elif ct == "link":
257|                 if child.text:
258|                     link = child.text.strip()
259|                 elif child.get("href"):
260|                     link = child.get("href", "")
261|             elif ct in ("description", "summary", "content") and child.text:
262|                 summary = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", child.text or "")
263|                 summary = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", summary).strip()[:500]
264|         if title:
265|             items.append({"title": title, "link": link, "summary": summary})
266|         if len(items) >= max_items:
267|             break
268|     return items

412| def provider_probe_due(
413|     state: dict[str, Any] | None,
414|     cadence_days: float = _PROVIDER_PROBE_DEFAULT_CADENCE_DAYS,
415|     *,
416|     now: datetime | None = None,

418|     """Cadence gate for the weekly deep provider probe (B2-106).
419| 
420|     Contract (pinned by tests/test_improve_provider_probe.py): due when the
421|     state key is missing, empty, or unparseable (a broken clock must not
422|     silence the probe forever: an unreadable ts re-arms the cadence), or
423|     when now - ts >= cadence_days. A fresh ts inside the window is not due.
424|     cadence_days <= 0 means always due (operator knob, not a footgun).
425|     """
426|     raw = ""
427|     try:
428|         raw = str((state or {}).get(_PROVIDER_PROBE_STATE_KEY) or "")
429|     except Exception:
430|         raw = ""
431|     if not raw:
432|         return True
433|     try:
434|         last = datetime.fromisoformat(raw)
435|     except ValueError:
436|         return True
437|     if last.tzinfo is None:
438|         last = last.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
439|     now_dt = now or _utc_now()
440|     return (now_dt - last).total_seconds() >= max(float(cadence_days), 0.0) * 86400.0

101| def ingest_cloud_handoffs(*, limit: int = 10) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
102|     """List unprocessed cloud handoffs (newest first)."""
103|     if not HANDOFF_DIR.is_dir():
104|         return []
105|     rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
106|     # UUID filenames are deliberately opaque and are not chronological.  The
107|     # old lexical sort could hide a just-written handoff behind ten older
108|     # records, making the mailbox look unwired.  Read the durable timestamp,
109|     # then apply the limit after sorting.
110|     for p in HANDOFF_DIR.glob(f"{CLOUD_PREFIX}*.json"):
111|         try:
112|             h = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
113|             h["_path"] = p.name
114|             rows.append(h)
115|         except Exception:
116|             continue
117|     rows.sort(key=lambda row: str(row.get("ts") or ""), reverse=True)
118|     return rows[: max(0, int(limit))]

1| """Janitor — autonomous prune + document to keep the environment lean and documented.
2| 
3| This is the standing "keep the house clean" job the operator wanted wired into the
4| autorun loop. It is PURE (no side effects beyond its own report) and CONSERVATIVE:
5| 
6|   Prune
7|     - temp dirs at project root matching  codex_*  and  *_temp
8|     - pytest scratch dirs under  agents/pytest-*
9|     - stale .tmp files under  memory/  (older than PRUNE_TMP_MIN_AGE_S)
10|     - best-effort: locked/in-use files are skipped (never crash the loop)
11| 
12|   Document
13|     - regenerate  memory/briefs/latest.md   (session_state_brief.write_brief)
14|     - regenerate  memory/ideas/LATEST.md    (idea_graph.write_latest_face)
15| 
16|   Guard
17|     - refuses to run while the operator is active (preferences.operator_status)
18|       or when the drainer/autonomy is disabled — so it never prunes under you.
19| 
20| Cadence is enforced by the caller (governor_autorun cadence); this module is the
21| unit of work. Every run appends a row to memory/runs/janitor_report.jsonl.
22| 
23| REST: POST /api/v1/janitor   -> run()
24|       GET  /api/v1/janitor   -> last report
25| CLI:  python -m mag.janitor [--dry] [--prune-only] [--document-only]
26| """
27| from __future__ import annotations
28| 
29| import json
30| import shutil
31| import sys
32| import time
33| from datetime import datetime, timezone
34| from pathlib import Path
35| from typing import Any
36| 
37| try:
38|     from config import ROOT
39| except ImportError:
40|     ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
41| 
42| sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
43| 
44| try:
45|     sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
46| except Exception:
47|     pass
48| 
49| REPORT_PATH = ROOT / "memory" / "runs" / "janitor_report.jsonl"
50| PRUNE_TMP_MIN_AGE_S = 86400  # only delete .tmp files older than 1 day
51| 
52| 
53| def _now() -> str:
54|     return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
55| 
56| 
57| def _append_report(row: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
58|     REPORT_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
59|     with REPORT_PATH.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
60|         f.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False, default=str) + "\n")
61| 
62| 
63| def last_report() -> dict[str, Any] | None:
64|     if not REPORT_PATH.is_file():
65|         return None
66|     lines = REPORT_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()
67|     for line in reversed(lines):
68|         line = line.strip()
69|         if not line:
70|             continue
71|         try:
72|             return json.loads(line)
73|         except json.JSONDecodeError:
74|             continue
75|     return None
76| 
77| 
78| def _guard() -> dict[str, bool]:
79|     """Refuse to prune/document under an active operator or a disabled drainer."""
80|     op_active = False
81|     drainer_ok = True
82|     try:
83|         from mag.preferences import operator_status
84|         op_active = bool(operator_status().get("operator_active"))
85|     except Exception:
86|         pass
87|     try:
88|         from mag.preferences import drainer_status
89|         drainer_ok = bool(drainer_status().get("autorun_allowed"))
90|     except Exception:
91|         pass
92|     return {"operator_active": op_active, "drainer_allowed": drainer_ok}
93| 
94| 
95| # ====================================================================
96| # PRUNE
97| # ====================================================================
98| def _rmtree_tolerant(p: Path) -> bool:
99|     try:
100|         if p.is_dir():
101|             shutil.rmtree(p, ignore_errors=True)
102|         elif p.is_file() or p.is_symlink():
103|             p.unlink(missing_ok=True)
104|         return not p.exists()
105|     except Exception:
106|         return False
107| 
108| 
109| def prune(*, dry: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
110|     removed: list[str] = []
111|     failed: list[str] = []
112|     freed_est = 0
113| 
114|     # 1. codex_* and *_temp dirs at project root
115|     for child in ROOT.iterdir():
116|         if not child.is_dir():
117|             continue
118|         name = child.name
119|         if name.startswith("codex_") or name.endswith("_temp"):
120|             if dry:
121|                 removed.append(str(child.relative_to(ROOT)))
122|                 continue
123|             if _rmtree_tolerant(child):
124|                 removed.append(str(child.relative_to(ROOT)))
125|             else:
126|                 failed.append(str(child.relative_to(ROOT)))
127| 
128|     # 2. pytest scratch dirs under agents/pytest-*
129|     agents = ROOT / "agents"
130|     if agents.is_dir():
131|         for child in agents.iterdir():
132|             if child.is_dir() and child.name.startswith("pytest-"):
133|                 if dry:
134|                     removed.append(str(child.relative_to(ROOT)))
135|                     continue
136|                 if _rmtree_tolerant(child):
137|                     removed.append(str(child.relative_to(ROOT)))
138|                 else:
139|                     failed.append(str(child.relative_to(ROOT)))
140| 
141|     # 3. stale .tmp files under memory/
142|     cutoff = time.time() - PRUNE_TMP_MIN_AGE_S
143|     mem = ROOT / "memory"
144|     if mem.is_dir():
145|         for child in mem.rglob("*.tmp"):
146|             try:
147|                 if child.stat().st_mtime < cutoff:
148|                     if dry:
149|                         removed.append(str(child.relative_to(ROOT)))
150|                         continue
151|                     if _rmtree_tolerant(child):
152|                         removed.append(str(child.relative_to(ROOT)))
153|                     else:
154|                         failed.append(str(child.relative_to(ROOT)))
155|             except Exception:
156|                 continue
157| 
158|     return {
159|         "removed": removed,
160|         "n_removed": len(removed),
161|         "failed": failed[:20],
162|         "n_failed": len(failed),
163|         "dry": dry,
164|     }
165| 
166| 
167| # ====================================================================
168| # DOCUMENT
169| # ====================================================================
170| def document(*, dry: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
171|     written: dict[str, str] = {}
172| 
173|     # 1. Regenerate the live session-state brief
174|     try:
175|         from mag.session_state_brief import write_brief
176|         if not dry:
177|             res = write_brief()
178|             written["briefs/latest.md"] = str(res.get("path", "?"))
179|         else:
180|             written["briefs/latest.md"] = "(dry)"
181|     except Exception as e:
182|         written["briefs/latest.md"] = f"error: {str(e)[:120]}"
183| 
184|     # 2. Regenerate the idea-graph LATEST face
185|     try:
186|         from mag.idea_graph import write_latest_face
187|         if not dry:
188|             p = write_latest_face()
189|             written["ideas/LATEST.md"] = str(p.relative_to(ROOT))
190|         else:
191|             written["ideas/LATEST.md"] = "(dry)"
192|     except Exception as e:
193|         written["ideas/LATEST.md"] = f"error: {str(e)[:120]}"
194| 
195|     return {"written": written, "dry": dry}
196| 
197| 
198| # ====================================================================
199| # RUN
200| # ====================================================================
201| def run(*, dry: bool = False, prune_only: bool = False, document_only: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
202|     guard = _guard()
203|     row: dict[str, Any] = {
204|         "schema": "janitor.v1",
205|         "ts": _now(),
206|         "dry": dry,
207|         "guard": guard,
208|     }
209| 
210|     # Refuse to actually prune while operator is active (safe; still allow doc).
211|     if not dry and guard.get("operator_active"):
212|         row["prune"] = {"skipped": "operator_active"}
213|         row["action"] = "skipped:operator_active"
214|         _append_report(row)
215|         return row
216| 
217|     if not document_only:
218|         row["prune"] = prune(dry=dry)
219|     if not prune_only:
220|         row["document"] = document(dry=dry)
221| 
222|     row["action"] = "prune" if prune_only else ("document" if document_only else "prune+document")
223|     if not dry:
224|         _append_report(row)
225|     return row
226| 
227| 
228| # ====================================================================
229| # CLI
230| # ====================================================================
231| def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
232|     import argparse
233|     ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Janitor — prune + document (lean & documented)")
234|     ap.add_argument("--dry", action="store_true", help="Report what would change, don't change")
235|     ap.add_argument("--prune-only", action="store_true")
236|     ap.add_argument("--document-only", action="store_true")
237|     ap.add_argument("--last", action="store_true", help="Print the last report")
238|     ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
239|     args = ap.parse_args(argv)
240| 
241|     if args.last:
242|         r = last_report()
243|         if args.json:
244|             print(json.dumps(r, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str))
245|             return 0
246|         print("LAST JANITOR REPORT")
247|         print(json.dumps(r, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str) if r else "(none)")
248|         return 0
249| 
250|     res = run(dry=args.dry, prune_only=args.prune_only, document_only=args.document_only)
251|     if args.json:
252|         print(json.dumps(res, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str))
253|         return 0
254| 
255|     print(f"JANITOR  {res['ts']}  action={res['action']} dry={res['dry']}")
256|     g = res.get("guard", {})
257|     print(f"  operator_active={g.get('operator_active')} drainer_allowed={g.get('drainer_allowed')}")
258|     if "prune" in res:
259|         p = res["prune"]
260|         if p.get("skipped"):
261|             print(f"  prune: skipped ({p['skipped']})")
262|         else:
263|             print(f"  prune: removed {p.get('n_removed', 0)}, failed {p.get('n_failed', 0)}")
264|             for r in (p.get("removed") or [])[:10]:
265|                 print(f"    - {r}")
266|     if "document" in res:
267|         for k, v in (res["document"].get("written") or {}).items():
268|             print(f"  doc: {k} -> {v}")
269|     return 0
270| 
271|

273|     raise SystemExit(main())

166| def probe(escalate: bool = True) -> dict:

175|                             "ok": ok, "why": why})
176|     after = _history()
177|

181|         if st == "DOWN":
182|             down.append(r)
183|         elif st == "FLAKING":

369|     watch/inbox/burn_wave_20260926/B2_81_ollama_truth_20260926.md): the old
370|     probe was a bare urllib.urlopen(timeout=0.6), which (a) inherits
371|     env/registry proxies, so a process launched with http_proxy set timed out
372|     against a LIVE daemon at 0.6s with no request ever reaching the server
373|     (reproduced: URLError timeout 0.61s via a dead proxy while /api/tags
374|     answered), and (b) had no retry, so load spikes past 600ms read as
375|     absent. 20 of the 21 verifiable lifecycle_gap:ollama rows show the server
376|     answering /api/tags 200 within 0-14s of the gap observation. Now:
377|     ProxyHandler({}) opener so proxies never intercept loopback, 2.0s timeout
378|     with two tries, then a raw socket-connect fallback (a listener means the
379|     daemon is on even if HTTP is wedged), and the cause names refused vs
380|     timeout so future rows carry their own verdict.
381|     """
382|     import socket
383|     import urllib.request
384| 
385|     last = "unknown"
386|     for _ in range(2):
387|         try:
388|             opener = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))
389|             with opener.open(OLLAMA_TAGS_URL, timeout=2.0) as r:
390|                 if r.status == 200:
391|                     return True, "11434"
392|                 last = f"http {r.status}"
393|         except Exception as exc:

470| def _simple_yaml(obj: Any, indent: int = 0) -> str:
471|     """Minimal YAML-ish dump (no PyYAML required)."""
472|     sp = "  " * indent
473|     if isinstance(obj, dict):
474|         lines = []
475|         for k, v in obj.items():
476|             if isinstance(v, (dict, list)):
477|                 lines.append(f"{sp}{k}:")
478|                 lines.append(_simple_yaml(v, indent + 1))
479|             else:
480|                 lines.append(f"{sp}{k}: {_yaml_scalar(v)}")
481|         return "\n".join(lines) + ("\n" if indent == 0 else "")
482|     if isinstance(obj, list):
483|         lines = []
484|         for item in obj:
485|             if isinstance(item, (dict, list)):
486|                 lines.append(f"{sp}-")
487|                 lines.append(_simple_yaml(item, indent + 1))
488|             else:
489|                 lines.append(f"{sp}- {_yaml_scalar(item)}")
490|         return "\n".join(lines)
491|     return f"{sp}{_yaml_scalar(obj)}"

494| def _yaml_scalar(v: Any) -> str:
495|     if v is None:
496|         return "null"
497|     if isinstance(v, bool):
498|         return "true" if v else "false"
499|     if isinstance(v, (int, float)):

39| def decompose(goal: str, n_bits: int) -> list[str]:
40|     """Decompose a goal into bite-sized deterministic bits (the memweave task fan-out)."""
41|     n = max(1, int(n_bits))
42|     words = [w for w in (goal or "").split() if w]
43|     if not words:
44|         return [f"[bit {i}] <empty goal>"] * n
45|     # deterministic round-robin bucketing into n bite-sized slices
46|     buckets: list[list[str]] = [[] for _ in range(n)]
47|     for i, w in enumerate(words):
48|         buckets[i % n].append(w)

56|     -> visual language. Deterministic + $0 (all local; no LLM spend)."""

62|     bits = decompose(goal, n_workers)
63|

65|     skeleton = "\n".join(bits)

68|     # 3) run the flock: agents seeded from each bit (cheap per-pixel) + O(N) spatial seams
69|     agents = [AgentSeed(id=i, pos=(float(i % 5), float(i % 3)),
70|                         role="worker", task=bits[i]) for i in range(n_workers)]

78|                       if s["nearest_d2"] is not None else 1.0} for s in seam_list

104| # ── CONSENSUS-ILLUSION GUARD (steal 2026-08-11) ─────────────────────────────────
105| # Memweave's #1 documented risk (grok-4.5 critique): CONSENSUS ILLUSION — correlated hallucinations
106| # counted as agreement. The fix (self-steal from gap_swarm_experiment.independent_witnesses +
107| # external agentswarm evidenceOverlap): agreement is only REAL if the agreeing witnesses are
108| # INDEPENDENT. N correlated answers ~= 1 opinion, not N. This guard reports the effective
109| # independent witness count so the weave never trusts a correlated consensus as a strong one.
110| 
111| def _tok(s: str) -> set[str]:
112|     return set((s or "").lower().split())
113| 
114| 
115| def consensus_quality(answers: list[str], *, independent: list[bool] | None = None,
116|                       rho: float | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
117|     """Effective independent agreement across the flock's answers (consensus-illusion guard).
118| 
119|     RESEARCH FIX (OX_SYNTHESIS consensus_illusion_detection, 2026-08-23): agreement is only REAL
120|     if the agreeing witnesses are INDEPENDENT. The old guard counted witnesses purely by token-
121|     overlap, so it could NOT tell two INDEPENDENTLY-CONSTRUCTED verifiers that byte-agree (the
122|     STRONG case) from one correlated opinion (an illusion) — it under-reported strong consensus.
123| 
124|     `independent` (optional, per-answer bool) supplies the construction-independence signal the
125|     token-overlap check cannot see. When provided, a byte-identical answer from an independently-
126|     constructed witness counts as an ADDITIONAL independent witness (strong). When omitted, the
127|     behavior is unchanged (token-overlap only) — a flock of identical answers stays correlated.
128| 
129|     `rho` (optional, mean pairwise error correlation in [0,1)) supplies the MEASURED correlation
130|     between agreeing witnesses (OX burn t0416). When provided, it converts raw agreement into
131|     effective independent witnesses via the closed-form rule:
132|         n* = n / (1 + (n - 1) * rho)
133|     At rho=0.9, ten agents give n* ~= 1.17 — ten correlated "unanimous" agents are worth barely
134|     more than one opinion. This is the measured-not-guessed rule: agreement carries evidential
135|     weight only in proportion to error independence.
136| 
137|     Verdict: 'strong' if >=2 effective independent witnesses agree; 'correlated_weak' if they
138|     collapse toward one opinion; 'single' otherwise. Deterministic + $0.
139|     """
140|     n = len(answers or [])
141|     if n == 0:
142|         return {"ok": True, "schema": "memweave.consensus.v1", "n_answers": 0,
143|                 "n_independent": 0, "n_effective": 0.0, "correlated": False, "verdict": "empty"}
144|     if independent is not None and len(independent) != n:
145|         raise ValueError("independent must be None or match len(answers)")
146|     if rho is not None:
147|         rho = float(rho)
148|         if not (0.0 <= rho < 1.0):
149|             raise ValueError("rho must be in [0,1)")
150|     # structural independent witnesses (token-overlap + explicit independence signal)
151|     wit: set[int] = set()
152|     for i in range(n):
153|         correlated = False
154|         ti = _tok(answers[i])
155|         for j in wit:
156|             tj = _tok(answers[j])
157|             if not ti or not tj:
158|                 continue
159|             ov = len(ti & tj) / len(ti | tj)
160|             if ov >= 0.6:
161|                 correlated = True
162|                 break
163|         if not correlated:
164|             wit.add(i)
165|         elif independent is not None and independent[i]:
166|             # explicit independence signal: a byte-identical answer from an independently-
167|             # constructed witness is a NEW independent voice, not a correlated echo (the strong case)
168|             if any(answers[i] == answers[j] and independent[j] for j in wit):
169|                 wit.add(i)
170|     n_ind = len(wit)
171|     # measured effective independent witnesses (correlation-adjusted), when rho is known
172|     if rho is not None:
173|         n_effective = n / (1 + (n - 1) * rho)
174|         eff = n_effective
175|     else:
176|         n_effective = float(n_ind)
177|         eff = n_ind
178|     verdict = ("strong" if eff >= 2 else
179|                "correlated_weak" if (eff < n and n >= 2) else
180|                "single")
181|     return {"ok": True, "schema": "memweave.consensus.v1", "n_answers": n,
182|             "n_independent": n_ind, "n_effective": round(n_effective, 4),
183|             "rho": rho, "correlated": n_ind < n, "verdict": verdict}
184|

172| def _sentences(text: str) -> list[str]:
173|     parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n+", text)
174|     return [p.strip() for p in parts if len(p.strip()) >= 25]
175| 
176| 
177| def _match(text: str, patterns: list[str]) -> list[str]:
178|     """Return distinct matching sentences for a pattern family (capped)."""
179|     sents = _sentences(text)
180|     hits: list[str] = []
181|     seen: set[str] = set()
182|     for pat in patterns:
183|         rx = re.compile(pat, re.IGNORECASE)
184|         for s in sents:
185|             if rx.search(s) and s not in seen:
186|                 seen.add(s)
187|                 hits.append(s)
188|     return hits
189| 
190| 
191| def _count(text: str, patterns: list[str]) -> int:
192|     """Count distinct matching sentences (clean count, not raw substring hits)."""
193|     return len(_match(text, patterns))
194|

196| def _map_lesson(correction: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
197|     """Map a correction to the standing law it trains (best keyword overlap; else unspecified)."""
198|     low = correction.lower()
199|     best, best_n = None, 0
200|     for row in _LESSON_MAP:
201|         n = sum(1 for kw in row["keywords"] if kw in low)
202|         if n > best_n:
203|             best, best_n = row, n
204|     if best is None or best_n == 0:
205|         return {"law": "unspecified", "text": "(no clear standing law)", "matched": []}
206|     return {"law": best["law"], "text": best["text"],
207|             "matched": [kw for kw in best["keywords"] if kw in low]}

210| def mine_session(session: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
211|     inv_evidence: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
212|     inv_hits: Counter = Counter()
213|     themes: Counter = Counter()
214|     register: Counter = Counter()
215|     corrections: list[str] = []
216|     refusals: list[str] = []
217|     for ev in session["events"]:
218|         c = (ev.get("content") or "").strip()
219|         if not c:
220|             continue
221|         kind = ev["kind"]
222|         if kind == "assistant.message":
223|             for inv in _INVARIANTS:
224|                 hits = _match(c, inv["signals"])
225|                 if hits:
226|                     inv_hits[inv["label"]] += len(hits)
227|                     inv_evidence.setdefault(inv["label"], [])
228|                     for h in hits:
229|                         if h not in inv_evidence[inv["label"]] and len(inv_evidence[inv["label"]]) < 4:
230|                             inv_evidence[inv["label"]].append(h)
231|             refusals.extend(_match(c, _REFUSAL_SIGNALS))
232|         elif kind == "user.message":
233|             corrections.extend(_match(c, _CORRECTION_SIGNALS))
234|             for reg in _REGISTER:
235|                 register[reg["label"]] += _count(c, reg["signals"])
236|         for theme in _THEMES:
237|             themes[theme["label"]] += _count(c, theme["signals"])
238|     tools: list[str] = []
239|     for ev in session["events"]:
240|         tools.extend(ev.get("tools") or [])
241|     # lesson-ledger for this session
242|     lessons = [_map_lesson(x) for x in corrections]
243|     lesson_agg: Counter = Counter(l["law"] for l in lessons)
244|     return {"source": session["source"], "n_events": session["n_events"],
245|             "summary": summarize_session(session),
246|             "invariant_hits": dict(inv_hits),
247|             "invariant_evidence": inv_evidence,

249|             "register": dict(register),
250|             "corrections_total": len(corrections),
251|             "corrections": corrections[:8],
252|             "refusals": refusals[:8],
253|             "lesson_ledger": dict(lesson_agg),
254|             "tools": Counter(tools)}

97| # (bus-guard lesson: a guard that flags the treaty's own currency defeats the treaty).

101| # ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
102| # Redaction
103| # ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
104| def _entropy(tok: str) -> float:
105|     """Shannon entropy per char (bits). Lowercase hex ~4.0; real keys ~5.8+."""
106|     if not tok:
107|         return 0.0
108|     import math
109|     counts: dict[str, int] = {}
110|     for ch in tok:
111|         counts[ch] = counts.get(ch, 0) + 1
112|     n = len(tok)
113|     return -sum((c / n) * math.log2(c / n) for c in counts.values())
114| 
115| 
116| def _is_content_hash(tok: str) -> bool:
117|     return bool(_HASH_OK.match(tok)) or (tok.isalnum() and len(tok) >= 32 and _entropy(tok) < 4.5
118|                                          and tok.islower())

121| def redact(text: str) -> tuple[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
122|     """Return (safe_text, ledger). Ledger records each replacement type + count (no raw secrets)."""
123|     ledger: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
124|     safe = text
125| 
126|     # 1) literals first (longest first) — identity + territory exact strings
127|     for literal, placeholder in sorted(_IDENTITY_MAP + _TERRITORY_MAP,
128|                                        key=lambda kv: -len(kv[0])):
129|         pat = re.compile(re.escape(literal), re.IGNORECASE)
130|         n = len(pat.findall(safe))
131|         if n:
132|             safe = pat.sub(placeholder, safe)
133|             ledger.append({"layer": "identity", "type": "literal", "target": placeholder,
134|                            "count": n})
135| 
136|     # 2) secret patterns
137|     for pattern, kind in _SECRET_PATTERNS:
138|         pat = re.compile(pattern)
139|         for m in pat.finditer(safe):
140|             tok = m.group(0).strip()
141|             # don't redact public content hashes / hex roots
142|             if kind == "secret:high-entropy" and _is_content_hash(tok):
143|                 continue
144|             safe = safe.replace(m.group(0), f"<redacted:{kind}>", 1)
145|             ledger.append({"layer": "secret", "type": kind, "target": f"<redacted:{kind}>",
146|                            "count": 1})
147| 
148|     # 3) identity regexes
149|     for pattern, placeholder, kind in _IDENTITY_RE:
150|         pat = re.compile(pattern, re.IGNORECASE)
151|         n = len(pat.findall(safe))
152|         if n:
153|             safe = pat.sub(placeholder, safe)
154|             ledger.append({"layer": "identity", "type": kind, "target": placeholder, "count": n})
155| 
156|     # merge + summarize ledger (dedupe identical (layer,type,target) rows)
157|     merged: dict[tuple[str, str, str], int] = {}
158|     for e in ledger:
159|         k = (e["layer"], e["type"], e["target"])
160|         merged[k] = merged.get(k, 0) + e["count"]
161|     final_ledger = [{"layer": l, "type": t, "target": p, "count": c}
162|                     for (l, t, p), c in sorted(merged.items(),
163|                                                key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0][1]))]
164|     return safe, final_ledger

170| def ingest_transcript(path: str | Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
171|     """Parse a VS Code session transcript JSONL into ordered, flat events.
172| 
173|     Each event: {kind, ts, speaker, content, tools}. We keep tool NAMES (the method — which tools
174|     were used) but drop tool ARGUMENTS (they carry paths/secrets/private specifics). The full
175|     arguments never enter the sanitized artifact — withheld by construction, not by regex.
176|     """
177|     events: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
178|     with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
179|         for line in fh:
180|             line = line.strip()
181|             if not line:
182|                 continue
183|             try:
184|                 ev = json.loads(line)
185|             except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
186|                 continue
187|             typ = ev.get("type", "")
188|             data = ev.get("data") or {}
189|             ts = ev.get("timestamp") or data.get("startTime") or ""
190|             base = {"kind": typ, "ts": ts}
191|             if typ == "session.start":
192|                 base["session_id"] = data.get("sessionId", "")
193|                 base["producer"] = data.get("producer", "")
194|             elif typ == "user.message":
195|                 base["speaker"] = "human"
196|                 base["content"] = (data.get("content") or "")
197|             elif typ == "assistant.message":
198|                 base["speaker"] = "agent"
199|                 base["content"] = (data.get("content") or "")
200|                 tools = [(tr.get("name") or "") for tr in (data.get("toolRequests") or [])
201|                          if tr.get("name")]
202|                 base["tools"] = [t for t in tools if t]  # names only; args withheld
203|             elif typ in ("assistant.turn_start", "assistant.turn_end",
204|                          "tool.execution_start", "tool.execution_complete"):
205|                 base["speaker"] = "agent"
206|             else:
207|                 continue
208|             events.append(base)
209|     return events

241| def transcript_text(session: dict[str, Any], *, prose_max: int = 3000,
242|                     tool_group_every: int = 15, total_cap: int = 60000) -> str:
243|     """Render a sanitized session as a CONDENSED, readable, honest transcript.
244| 
245|     The raw transcripts are dominated by mechanical tool-call events (thousands per long
246|     session). That is noise, not a window. So we:
247|       * keep EVERY human turn (the operator's steering/corrections — the gold), truncated,
248|       * keep the agent's substantive prose (real reasoning), truncated,
249|       * collapse tool-only stretches into compact grouped "[worked via tools: ...]" lines,
250|       * cap the whole session so it reads instead of burying the reasoning in tool-spam.
251| 
252|     This is DETERMINISTIC and EXTRACTIVE — we only drop mechanical noise and keep real text;
253|     nothing is fabricated or re-worded (honesty: never claim first unless from data).
254|     """
255|     lines: list[str] = []
256|     tool_batch: list[str] = []
257|     total = 0
258| 
259|     def _flush_tools() -> None:
260|         nonlocal tool_batch, total
261|         if not tool_batch:
262|             return
263|         uniq = list(dict.fromkeys(tool_batch))
264|         line = f"AGENT [worked via tools: {', '.join(uniq)}]"
265|         lines.append(line)
266|         total += len(line)
267|         tool_batch = []
268| 
269|     for ev in session["events"]:
270|         kind = ev["kind"]
271|         if kind in ("session.start", "assistant.turn_start", "assistant.turn_end",
272|                     "tool.execution_start", "tool.execution_complete"):
273|             continue
274|         if kind == "user.message":
275|             _flush_tools()
276|             c = (ev.get("content") or "").strip()
277|             if c:
278|                 line = f"HUMAN — {c[:prose_max]}"
279|                 lines.append(line)
280|                 total += len(line)
281|         elif kind == "assistant.message":
282|             c = (ev.get("content") or "").strip()
283|             tools = ev.get("tools") or []
284|             if c:
285|                 _flush_tools()
286|                 tline = f"  [tools: {', '.join(tools)}]" if tools else ""
287|                 line = f"AGENT — {c[:prose_max]}{tline}"
288|                 lines.append(line)
289|                 total += len(line)
290|             elif tools:
291|                 tool_batch.extend(tools)
292|                 if len(tool_batch) >= tool_group_every:
293|                     _flush_tools()
294|         if total >= total_cap:
295|             _flush_tools()
296|             lines.append("… (mechanical work continues — window capped for readability; "
297|                          "see the raw source / ledger for the full record)")
298|             break
299|     _flush_tools()
300|     return "\n\n".join(lines) if lines else "(no substantive turns)"

303| def summarize_session(session: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
304|     """A compact, deterministic per-session summary: counts + the method's tool fingerprint."""
305|     human = prose = toolonly = 0
306|     tools: list[str] = []
307|     for ev in session["events"]:
308|         kind = ev["kind"]
309|         if kind == "user.message" and (ev.get("content") or "").strip():
310|             human += 1
311|         elif kind == "assistant.message":
312|             if (ev.get("content") or "").strip():
313|                 prose += 1
314|                 tools.extend(ev.get("tools") or [])
315|             elif ev.get("tools"):
316|                 toolonly += 1
317|                 tools.extend(ev.get("tools") or [])
318|     from collections import Counter
319|     top = Counter(tools).most_common(8)
320|     return {"human_turns": human, "agent_prose": prose, "tool_only_events": toolonly,
321|             "top_tools": [{"tool": t, "uses": n} for t, n in top]}
